name: @w6w-apps/onepassword
description: Read and manage 1Password vault items through a self-hosted Connect server, and read the account's audit trail through the Events API.

w6w.longDescription:
1Password puts a self-hosted Connect server's vault items — and, separately, an account's audit trail — into a workflow. Vault items can be listed and read, one field's value fetched by name, items created and updated with a targeted patch rather than a full replace, and attachments listed and downloaded; the account's audit events, item-usage log and sign-in attempts are read through the separate Events API.

This app reads secrets, so it is built around not surfacing them by accident. Reading an item's structure returns its fields and labels with values redacted; getting an actual secret value is a deliberate, separate step — either revealing everything on the item or, better, fetching exactly one named field so the rest of the item's secrets never enter the run's data at all. No action logs a field value, item title or filename.

Connect and Events are two entirely separate credentials with no overlap: a Connect token is scoped to specific vaults and can only read and write items, while an Events Reporting token reads the audit trail and cannot touch a single item — deliberately two auth methods rather than one combined credential that could both read every secret and read the record of having done so. Updating an item uses a patch rather than a full replace, since a full replace silently deletes any field left out of the request; deleting an item archives it rather than destroying it, since the credential it held keeps working wherever it was already used.
